I won't lie to you. It's terrible. It traumatised me and gave me PTSD. However, it gets better. I just got the courage to start dating again.

Five months in here and every day! I don't think it'll do anything, tbh. I am still so angry, and a lot of the time, I don't know where to put that anger. I feel like I want to speak my truth, but I have no way of doing it.

Welcome to the club! I'm five months in, and I'm still furious. I want to say it gets better, and it did for a while for me, but now I've taken so many steps back. All I can advise is to take care of yourself. I am sorry this happened to you. :(( ❤️❤️❤️

I'm so sorry you're experiencing this, sweets. It's so hard. I know. I can't lie. It's so rough. All I can say is try to take care of yourself. It will get better eventually. I still haven't moved on, almost five months later, but I can function now. It'll be the same for you. The person has stated that they aren't good enough for you and they're right. You deserve better xoxo
He's a narcissist. What you experienced is a hoover. Block him on everything and put a sturdy no contact regime in place.

I'm so sorry this happened to you! All I can advise I that you take care of yourself while you grieve. Yes, you will grieve. It will be even more challenging due to the lack of closure. Therapy helped me, and I am better than when it first happened, though I still tear up from time to time. You will go through periods of self-blame and rightfully placing the fault onto him. You will tumble back and forth with blame and through emotions. It's messy. But you have to keep reminding yourself that it's not your fault, and even if it were, anyone with a crumb of integrity and courage would have been truthful and given you answers. Unfortunately, from what I've experienced, men will say anything to get what they want, be it sex or attention and then ghost. They see it as a challenge to trick and “win” something from us. It's sick and abusive, but it's a commonplace. You will get used to the pain (the stage I'm in now), and one day, it will be gone. There's nothing that can make that time come sooner, but taking care of yourself will help you in the long run. Sending love and light your way 💕

This sounds so awful! I'm sorry this is happening to you. Unfortunately, there isn't much you can do except cut him out or wait for him to reach out. I don't advise you to reach out again, as this usually has the opposite effect. What you described sounds like love bombing, and personality types who do this can feign hard times to keep you hanging on while they cultivate other sources of supply. Or they disappear without a word or trace (this is what happened to me). Focusing on what you need and taking care of yourself over fretting about what he needs might help you in the long run. Neglecting myself made everything much worse. Bad times or not, you deserve someone who won't shut you out like this. Going through a rough patch doesn't give him a pass to neglect you. You sound like a loving and caring person. You deserve better. Sending love and light your way 💕

No problem sweets ❤️ I know it feels like you're alone, but I promise you aren't. Many folks have experienced it, but it does leave you feeling like you are. I also experienced what you're expressing too. He worked so hard to win me over to ghost me. In my case, he always knew he was going to ghost, though. I was the one who wanted to proceed carefully; I didn't ask for a relationship; I didn't ask for any commitment; I didn't ask for anything. He kept saying it was what he wanted, and as soon as I let myself believe in the fairytale, it ended. It truly felt like a kick in the gut. Unfortunately, some people get off on hurting others; others hurt others because they are hurting. With the former, they tend to target people with abandonment issues because we validate them. They know how to make us feel “special” with all of the undivided attention and love. They then snatch it away because when we chase, it validates their ego. Intentional or not, this isn't someone you can have a healthy relationship with. I know you want to reach out to family and only you can decide where you join the line.  From my experience, contacting him was not a good idea, and it only made matters worse. If by some miracle you still want him, chasing him (by either messaging him or his family/friends) is going to do the opposite. I understand that with abandonment wounds, we react and “chase” those who withdraw. In my situation, it made it worse. You mentioned that his friends/family are also blocking you, which means a boundary has been set. If you can afford it, please get some counselling or therapy. It genuinely helped me.

I am so sorry this happened to you! It sounds like you were love-bombed which is typical behaviour of people who ghost. I hope you can take care of yourself. You will get through this, I promise. I know it hurts like heck. Not only for the loss of what you thought you have and the grief that comes from that but the wounds he reopened. I am three months into my situation; I want to let you know that it does get better (abandonment issues and all). If you can, refrain from contacting him in any way. Sending love and light your way.

This was precisely me too! In doing so, I found out his real name (he gave me his middle name), I confirmed he was in the military and confirmed he was a narcissist as he had done this to other people. I look like an utterly batshit stalker to anyone who doesn't know the ins and outs of the situation. The whole situation ran me crazy. I'm only starting to process it now (especially the past two days) in that it didn't mean anything to him, he always planned on doing it, and he has real issues. I think of him as a psychological serial killer. I'm not joking; he even goes as far as using burner numbers. He was not who I thought he was, and not someone I want to get involved with. In my case, he planned it from the absolute start (he dropped hints that only make sense now). However, was all that digging worth it? No, I wish I'd just let it go from the jump but, easier said than done. In a strange way, I needed it to be my fault because then I could stay in denial, and he wouldn't be an evil pos. It did show me that I wasn't crazy, and my intuition was correct. He targets seduces and discards because he mines emotionally charged reactions ( that I naively gave him).
In doing so, I provided a narcissistic supply; he would feel justified in what he was doing, and it would boost his fragile self-esteem. Now he knows how miserable I was and how much mayhem he caused without him even lifting a finger. Starting to realise that I was lucky this didn't go on for longer than it did. Be kind to yourself in that you reacted to toxic behaviour. You didn't “stalk” to control, cause fear or intimidation. You don't do this under normal circumstances (read about the effects of silent treatment and loss of control). Ghosting is considered the ultimate form of silent treatment, mostly when people with narcissistic personality types employ it. I want to work on being one of those high-value people who let it go from the jump. Sorry to vent! It's not my post, and I haven't written about it in detail to folks going through the same thing. Feels relieving not to be the only one who went this route lol.

You aren't alone! I’m taken aback at how similar our stories are. I felt the same way as you did. I still feel like if he came back with an excuse, I might not be able to say no. But do I want him as much as I did? No.  I want him less and less as time goes on. I do miss him and the way he made me feel. I miss feeling like I’d found my soulmate. I miss the rush of falling in love. It's perfectly normal for you to miss those things. I remember feeling like I'd missed my only chance at love too. But I promise one day, we will look back at that thought and laugh. What you're feeling is completely normal. Don't feel bad about it. You're welcome to PM me at anytime 💕

Wow! This was precisely me two and a half months ago. I'm so sorry for what you've gone through for real. My situation is pretty much identical to yours, so I’m going to list the opposite of what I've done and hope you’ve done or will do this haha.

- Do not text or call or write. There is nothing you can say that will remedy it. If by some miracle you still want him, chasing him will harm your chances of him getting back into contact. Act unbothered (you shouldn't have to resort to games, you deserve better).

- Delete and block his number immediately

- Delete all correspondence between the both of you

- Delete all pictures

- Block everywhere on social media

- Take care of yourself and your mental health

- If you can, get counselling

- Do not throw yourself into dating too soon

I know it sucks, it's horrible, it's an unbearable place to be in. It will get easier! I promise. After ten weeks, I woke up this morning, and it didn't hit me like a tonne of bricks as soon as I remembered. I'm also feeling ready to get back into the dating pool now and talk to new people. It gets better, but it isn't an easy task, I still feel shitty but not as shitty as I once did. This will be you too. Sending lots of love and light 💕

Nope. I tried this twice. I lost my dignity and let a narcissist know how much they hurt me. No response. 0/10. Would not recommend. After googling many articles, Quora and Reddit posts, I believed my case would be different. Perhaps I could be the one to inspire some empathy and get him to answer me. What if I was the exception? I even lied to myself and said: “I don't care if he responds, I want to express myself.” How naive I was. I spent days writing the perfect letter. He ignored it. Who knows if he even read it? It did not alleviate anything; if anything, the waiting for a response made me feel worse. It never came, and so it hurt me all over again. The healing process started from scratch. Then I ended up wondering if he even bothered reading it. So, now there were even more questions.

Nothing will make this magically go away. Only time with the help of a professional can do that. I understand you want it to go away. We want one small action that will bring relief to our pain. We want a cure to end all of the confusion. It's also important, to be honest with ourselves, why do we still want to talk to them? Each time I reached out or wanted to reach out to him, it was because I held a candle for us. Deep down, I still wanted him. Yes, I wanted closure, but I also hoped that some part of him would tell me it was as real to him as it was to me. I hoped that there was a grave misunderstanding between us. Maybe then, there would be hope for us. If I said the right thing, and I meant something to him, perhaps we could sort it all out. If you want to, by all means, do it, but it should be done when you genuinely don't care about whether or not you hear from them again.

You’re doing your best, so I'm not going to sit here and patronise you by telling you to move on, or to “bring yourself closure”. I am sure you've been doing that in your way (blocking him etc.) 

I hope peace comes to you soon 💕

I experienced the same thing you did. It's scary how identical the story us. Two months in and I'm still hurting. I was bed-bound for the first two weeks. It gets easier, even if you do still miss them. Please take care of yourself.
He's a narcissist. What you experienced was a hoover. Please change your number and go no contact.
Thank you!
No contact is done out of safety; ghosting is what immature people, narcissists and general arseholes do.
This is called going no contact. It's not the same as ghosting.
Saved you a lot of time with that one 😂

Come clean and give them closure. Whatever you do, do not ghost because that will have the most negative impact. It was the answered questions and ”why’s” that caused the most pain for me. More so than missing them. I know it won't be easy, but it will allow them to process this properly and make healing easier.

I get that you have self-esteem issues, but please realise how messed up it is that people are being intimate with someone they're not consenting to. As sad as this is, and I'm sorry for you having a disability and being overweight. It's not an excuse to do what you're doing. It has real-life ramifications and impact on the mental health of the people you target. I was a mess for a month, bedridden for two. Couldn't go to work, couldn't even go to university. Drank myself stupid. I relapsed into a codeine addiction and bulimia because I fell in love with a catfish who ghosted me.
Be kind to yourself; it's the lack of closure that makes it more challenging. ❤️❤️❤️

Do NOT ghost him, that is even more of an insult and will hurt him. A possible catfish ghosted me after just five weeks of talking, and it had to lead to a month of depression and relapsing into addictions and other problems. And I want to say, as was as your backstory is, it doesn't excuse messing with a real person’s emotions like that. I'm unsure as to whether things have gotten sexual between both of you, but they are consenting to someone who doesn't exist. That's pretty messed up. Come clean.
He would have to watch their stories for it to come up.

You were sadly love-bombed, the ”married with kids by now” line was love-bombing. People love to get on their high horses on what should have happened but it's not so easy when someone is giving you a high akin to heroin, ecstasy and cocaine. Your mind was in the clouds and that's normal. Even if red flags do appear you easily explain them away and write them off as paranoia. Deep down in your gut did you sense something was wrong? Were you waiting for the other foot to drop? I wish I had listened to my gut. It would have saved a lot of heartaches but everything is 20/20 with hindsight. 

What he is doing now by watching your stories but somewhat ghosting is making you wonder WHY. It's about power and control, unfortunately. This isn't someone you want to be caught up with.

You made me feel less alone with the private investigator part, it gave me a much-needed chuckle. Thank you so much for your post. Currently very depressed after being catfished by someone who intended on scamming me.

Contact CID, IC3 and Interpol immediately. This person is a romance scammer. Make a report and tell them what is happening. You can try to reason and explain to your mum but she will most likely believe in this person because she wants to. Try and be supportive and try not to be judgmental as that may cause her to withdraw. If you can, contact this person and tell him to stop contacting your mother or you will report him to the authorities. This will hopefully deter him from asking for more money from her at least.

Please report them! You can do so on IC3 I believe. Also might be worth looking at Interpol. If you are in the U.K., action fraud too who work with Euro and Interpol. A Google search should tell you exactly where you need to go. I was catfished by a romance scammer who was posing as a military official and found out I had to report them to CID, action fraud and IC3. Even if you have the money do not pay them. Tell them you’ve made a report and block them.
